tiles: Studying the Bauhaus and its flat design language
Primary color, simple shape, quiet confidence
challenge: A lot of what we think of as 'modern graphic design' traces back to flat Bauhaus work — posters, covers, textiles — and I wanted to actually sit with that lineage rather than just absorb it secondhand from everything built on top of it.
approach: I read into the flat-design side of the Bauhaus (the posters and applied arts more than the architecture), then drafted a lot of variations built on primary color and simple shape. I kept the ones that felt warm and considered rather than cold or nostalgic.
result: A friendly, bright set of pieces that I enjoy looking at. They're available as prints for anyone who likes that kind of cheerful, grown-up flatness on a wall.
